title: Geometrically connected generic fibre spreads on an irreducible base
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a finite type morphism of schemes [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Assume $S$ is irreducible with generic point $\eta$ and the fibre morphism $X_\eta\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(\eta)$ is geometrically connected [def-pc-scheme-fibre, def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. Then there is an open $W\subseteq S$ containing $\eta$ such that $X_s\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ is geometrically connected for every $s\in W$. No reducedness, noetherianity, quasi-separatedness, rational point, or section is assumed.

proof.text: Obtain the finite closed irreducible generic cover, the open W and the auxiliary irreducible covers with preserved intersection edges from generic incidence spreading. This result assumes no generic connectedness.

Geometric connectedness of the generic fibre implies ConnectedSpace for its L-pullback by Mathlib.pullback_of_geometrically. Prove finite_closed_cover_paths: if one index cannot reach another, split the generic fibre into the finite closed unions of reachable and unreachable components. They cover and are both nonempty, so generic connectedness forces an intersection. Such an intersection is an edge reaching an unreachable index, a contradiction. This topological argument is fully proved in Lean in the private helper.

The nonempty connected generic pullback and its cover give a nonempty index type. For s in W and any K-test fibre, obtain Z,p,B. Irreducibility makes each B_i connected; monotonicity of ReflTransGen transfers every generic graph path to the B-intersection graph. Mathlib.IsConnected.iUnion_of_reflTransGen makes their union connected, hence Z is ConnectedSpace. The surjective continuous p gives ConnectedSpace of the K-test fibre by Function.Surjective.connectedSpace. Mathlib.geometrically_iff_of_isClosedUnderIsomorphisms and geometricallyConnected_iff finish.

proof_origin.note: Geometric incidence spreading is split off; the finite closed-cover graph argument, path transport, connected union and surjective descent are fully proved in Lean. Removing empty generic intersections is unnecessary.

mathlib_searches.query: A finite type scheme morphism with geometrically connected generic fibre has geometrically connected fibres on a nonempty open subset

lean.statement:
theorem exists_open_geometricallyConnected_fibres_of_generic {X S : Scheme.{u}}
    [IrreducibleSpace S] (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f]
    (hη : GeometricallyConnected (f.fiberToSpecResidueField (genericPoint S))) :
    ∃ W : Set S, IsOpen W ∧ genericPoint S ∈ W ∧
      ∀ s ∈ W, GeometricallyConnected (f.fiberToSpecResidueField s)
